information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities,

to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

( Page 3, clause 0.3 ) — Insert the following new clause after 0.3 and 
renumber the subsequent clause: 

'0.4 A scheme of labelling environment friendly products with the ECO logo 
has been introduced at the instance of the Ministry of Environment and 
Forests (MEF), Government of India. The ECO-Mark is being administered 
by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) under the BIS Act, 1986 as per the 
Resolutions No. 71 dated 21 February 1991 and No. 425 dated 28 October 
1992 published in the Gazette of the Government of India. For a product to 
be eligible for marking with the ECO logo, it shall also carry the ISI Mark of 
the BIS besides meeting additional environment friendly requirements. For 
this purpose the Standard Mark would be a single mark being a combination 
of the ISI Mark and the ECO logo. 

This amendment is based on the gazette Notification No. 170 dated 18 May 
1996 for plastic products as environment friendly products published in the 
Gazette of the Government of India. This amendment is, therefore, being 
issued to this standard to include environment friendly requirements for 
Plastic containers for pharmaceutical use : Part 1 Other than parenteral and 
ophthalmic preparations * 

( Page 4, clause 4.3.4 ) — Insert the following new clause after 4.3.4 and 
renumber the subsequent clauses:

performance prescribed.

^APPENDIX H 

( Clause A A ) 

METHOD OF TEST FOR COMPATIBILITY OF 
POLYETHYLENE CONTAINERS 

H-l. PRINCIPLE 

H-1.1 Pieces of polyethylene material with which the container is made are 
treated at an elevated temperature with the liquid which the container 
is intended to contain. The compatibility tests shall be carried out in 
accordance with H'3.1 and H-3.2 if the contents to be packed are liquid 
preparations. In case of dry powdered pharmaceuticals the method given 
in H-3.2 only shall be applicable. 

H-2. TEST SPECIMEN 

H-2.1 Material — Three test pieces of approximately equal size and 
having an area of not less than 15 cm« shall be cut from any convenient 
part of the container. Each test piece shall be cleaned, wiped and dried. 
It shall be measured for length, width and thickness to the nearest 005 mm 
and weighed to the nearest milligram. 



H-2.2 Container — Six samples of specific container intended for packing 
of particular product shall be tested in accordance with the procedure 
given in H-3.2. 

H-3, PROCEDURE 

H-3.1 Testing of Material — The liquid which is intended to be filled 
in the contahier shall be introduced into a glass vessel and test pieces 
completely immersed, avoiding unnecessary, contact with the other pieces 
or the walls of the glass vessel. Wlieie the density of plastics material is 
less than that of the liquid, small weights inert to the liquid, may be used 
to prevent the test pieces from either floating or curling. The test shall be 
carried out continuously over 28 days at a temperature of 50 ^ 2^C. 
The liquid and the test pieces shall be thoroughly agitated every 21 hours. 

After the required test period has elapsed, the test pieces shall be 
removed from the liquid, suitably cleaned, dried, weighed and measured. 

H-3.2 Testing of Container — In order to assess the compatibility of 
the container, the container shall be filled with the product to the nominal 
capacity, sealed and capped in the manner intended and tested at any one 
of the following conditions, depending upon the thermolabile character- 
istic of the product being tested: 

a) 50 db 2^*0 for a period of 28 days, 

b) 37 lb 2^0 for a period of 3 months, 

c) 27 ± 2X for 1/3 of th^ anticipated shelf life period, and 

d) 37 ± 2°C and 75 ± 5 percent relative humidity for 3 months 
( for preparations other than liquids ). 

H-3.2.1 The above test conditions are intended to serve as a guideline 
for usage of the container. However, a shelf life storage test at 27 ± 2^C 
or at ambient temperature should be carried out till the anticipated 
shelf life period of ihe product in order to confirm the suitability of the 
Container. 

H.4. TEST RESULTS AND INTERPRETATION 

H-4*i Material — At the end of the test period any change in weight, 
dimension or alterations in other characteristics, such as colour, blooming, 
etc, shall be used for determining the suitability of the container for the 
intended purpose. 

H-4.2 Containers — At the end of the test period, containers shall be 
examined for the following: 

a) Visible cracks, if any; 

b) Change in colour; 



c) Change in weight; and 

d) Change in shape. 

H-4.2.1 In the event of any sign of crack, the container shall be deemed 
to be unsuitable for use for the particular product. Any change in weight 
or shape or both shall be used by the manufacturer and purchaser to 
determine the suitability of the container. A very slight change in colour 
shall be considered insignificant. 

H-4.2.2 In addition, the contents shall be tested to ensure that it meets 
the house specification of the pharmaceutical manufacturer and shall be 
substantially free from foreign odour and taste. '

ISt7803(nirCl).1975 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR PLASTIC CONTAINERS 
FOR PHARMACEUTICAL USE 

PART I OTHER THAN PARENTERAL AND 
OPHTHALMIC PREPARATIONS 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part I ) was adopted by the Indian Standards 
Institution on 29 September 1975, after the draft finalized by the Plastic 
Containers Sectional Committee had been approved by the Marine, Cargo 
Movement and Packaging Division Council. 

0,2 With the growth of indigenous plastics packaging industry, plastic 
containers are replacing conventional containers made of materials, such as 
glass, metal, etc. Plastic containers are also being increasingly used for 
pharmaceutical trade. 

0.3 The package requirements for pharmaceutical preparations can broadly 
be classified into following two catagories, depending upon their use and 
requirements: 

a) Parenteral and ophthalmic preparations, and 

b) Other than parenteral and ophthalmic preparations. 

0.3.1 Since the containers for parenteral and ophthalmic preparations 
have to meet some extra requirements, it was felt necessary to cover the 
containers for above purposes in two parts of this standard. Therefore, 
Part II covers containers for parenteral and ophthalmic preparations. 

0*4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, express- 
ing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard ( Part I ) prescribes requirements for plastic containers 
for pharmaceutical use excluding parenteral and ophthalmic preparations. 



^Rules for rounding off numerical values ( rtvised ), 

3 



I8t7803(PartI).1975 

2. TERMINOLOGY 

2.1 For the purpose of this standard, definitions given in IS : 7019-1973* 
shall apply. 

3. REaUHtEMENTS 

3.1 Material — Only virgin plastic material, which is practically odourless, 
shall be used in the manufacture of the containers or any accessory product. 
Pigments used, if any, shall be those which are approved for the purpose 
of colouring plastics. 

3*2 Sise and Design • — The size, shape and design of the container shall 
be as agreed to between the purchaser and the vendor. 

4. PERFORMANCE TESTS 

4*1 Leakage Test — There shall be no signs of leakage when the container 
filled with water and fitted with aU the prescribed closures is kept inverted 
at ambient temperature for a period of 24 hours. 

4.2 Collapsibility Test — A container shall, by collapsing inwards during 
use, yield at least 90 percent of its nominal contents at the required rate of 
flow at ambient temperature. 

NoTB — This test is applicable when the containers used are of squeeze-bottle 
type. 

4«3 Container Material Testa — These tests shall be performed only on 
material obtained from containers before filling. 

4.3.1 Clarity of Aqueous Extract — An aqueous extract prepared in accor- 
dance with A-2.2 shall be colourless and free from turbidity. 

Note — Applicable only when the containers are used for liquid orals. 

4«3.2 Water-Soluble Impurities Content*— The impurities in an aqueous 
extract prepared in accordance with A*2«2 shall not exceed the appropriate 
limits given in Table 1. 

4J.3 Non-volatile Residue — The non-volatile residue of the aqueous 
extract when tested in accordance with Appendix B shall not exceed 
12*5 mg. 

4.3.4 p// Value — The ^H value of an aqueous extract prepared in 
accordance with A-2*2 shall be within the range of 4*0 to 7*75, and when 
5 percent of a 0*9 percent ( m x » ) aqueous solution of sodium chloride is 
added to the* extract the change in j^H value shall not exceed 1 unit. 

NoTB — Applicable only when the containers are used for liquid preparations.

NoTB — Not applicable to containers used for tablets, capsules, granules and 
powder, other than for dental preparations. 

5. PACaUNG AND MARKING 

5.1 Packing — The containers shall be delivered packed in acceptable 
outer packages. Only containers of the same nominal capacity and bearing 
the same batch identification shall be packed together in one package. 

5.2 Marking — The following information shall appear in legible and 
indelible marking on each container: 

a) The name or trade name or trade-mark of the manufacturer, and 

b) The batch identification. 

5.2.1 The containers may also be marked with the ISI Certification 
Mark. 

NoTB — The use of the ISI Certification Mark is ffovemed by the provuions of the 
Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regula- 
tions made thereunder. The ISI mark on products covered by an Indian Standard 
conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements 
of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control 
which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer. ISI marked 
products are also continuously checked by ISl for conformity to that standard as a 
further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the ISI 
Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained 
from the Indian Standards Institution. 

6. SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 

6*1 Lot • — All the containers of the same size, shape and design manufac- 
tured from the same raw materials under similar conditions of production! 
in a consignment, shall constitute a lot. 



nt7m3(PftrtI).197S

determine its conformity to the requirements of the specification. 

6.2 Number of Samples •— The number of containers to be selected in the 
sample from a lot shall depend upon the size of the lot and shall be in 
accordance with col 1, 2 and 4 of Table 2.

63 Selectl<Mi of Sample — - The samples shall be selected at random from

6*4 The containers selected in accordance with 6.2 ( Table 2, col 2 } shall 
be tested for leakage and coUapsibility {see 4.1 and 4,2). A container 
failing in any of the two tests will be considered as defective. A lot shall be 
considered as having satisfied the requirements of the standard only if 
the number of containers found defective in the sample does not exceed the 
number of permissible defectives given in col 3 of Table 2. 

6.5 The containers selected in the sample according to 6.2 ( Table 2, col 4 ) 
shall be individually tested for all the requirements of material ( see 4.3.1, 
4.3«2> 4«3«3 and 4Ji.4 ). A container failing in any one or more of the tests 
shall be considered as defective. A lot shall he considered as having satisfied 
the requirements of material only if all the containers tested in the sample 
pass all the tests individually.

APPENDIX A 

( Clauses 4.3.1, 4.3.2 and 4.3.4 ) 

METHOD OF PREPARATION OF SAMPLES AND EXTRACTS 

A-l. APPARATUS AND REAGENTS 

A-1.1 Unless otherwise stated, use only borosilicate glassware, analytical 
grade reagents and double distilled water from an all-glass distilling 
apparatus. 

A-1.2 Clean all glassware with chromosulphuric acid and rinse thoroughly 
with water. Clean other apparatus thoroughly using suitable deteigents. 

A-2. PROCEDURE 

A-2.1 Preparation of Sample — Select unlabelled, unmarked and non- 
laminated portions from suitable containers, taken at random, sufficient to 
yield a total area of sample required, taking into account the surface area 
of both sides. Cut these portions into strips, none of which have a total 
area of more than 20 cm*. Wash the strips, free from extraneous matter 
by shaking them in a flask with at least two separate portions of water for 
about 30 seconds in each case, then draining off the water thoroughly. 
NoTB — Do not wipe the sample or wash it with detergents. 

A-2.2 Preparation of Extract — Select, cut up and wash as prescribed 
in A-2.1 portions of the samples with a total surface area of 1 250 cm*. 
Transfer to a 500-ml flask, add 250 ml of water, cover the neck with an 
inverted glass beaker and autoclave at 12rC for 30 minutes ( preferably in 
autoclave that enables the charge to be cooled rapidly, after autoclaving, to 
a room temperature ). 

A-2.2«l Autoclave simultaneously a blank consisting of 250 ml of water. 

APPENDIX B 

( Clause 4.3.3 ) 

METHOD OF DETERMINATION OF NON-VOLATHE RESIDUE 
OF AQiUEOUS EXTRACTS 

B-1. PROCZDURE 

B-1.1 Pipette 100 ml of the aqueous extract prepared in accordance 
with A-2.2 into a dried and tared evaporating dish; evaporate to dryness 
on a water-bath and dry the residue to constant weight at 105**G. 



ISt7803(PartI).1975 

APPENDIX G 

[Table h It€m{i)] 

METHOD OF LIMIT TEST FOR OXIDIZABLE MATTER IN 
AQ^UEOUS EXTRACT 

G-l. REAGENTS 

G-1.1 Potassium Permanganate Soltttion — 0*01 N> accurately stan- 
dardized. 

&1.2 Dilate Sulphuric Acid — approximately 16 percent (vlv)y aqueous 
dilution of concentrated sulphuric acid. 

CS-1.3 Potassium Iodide ( KI ) 

CS-1.4 Starch Indicator — > I percent, aqueous. 

G-1.5 Sodium Thiosulphate Solution — 001 N, standardized against 
the potassium permanganate solution. 

&2. PROCEDURE 

C*2*l Pipette into the first of two 250-ml conical flasks ( marked 1 ) 20 ml 
of the aqueous extract of the sample ( see A-2.2 ) into the second ( marked 
2 ) 20 ml of the blank ( see A-2.2.1 ). Pipette into each flask 20 ml of the 
potassium permanganate solution, add I'O ml of the dilute sulphuric acid 
and boil for exactly 3 minutes. Cool the flask rapidly and add to each 
approximately 0*10 g of the potassium iodide and 5 drops of the starch 
indicator. Back titrate the liberated iodine in flasks 1 and 2 with the 
sodium thiosulphate solution and call the 2 volumes of sodium thiosulphate 
solution used A and B respectively. 

C-3. TEST RESULT 

C-3.1 Result oC B' minus result of* A* is the quantity of potassium per- 
manganate reduced. Total quantity of potassium permanganate solution 
used for 10 ml of aqueous extract should not be more than I ml. 

APPENDIX D 

[ Table 1, Item (ii) ] 

METHOD OF LIMIT TEST FOR SULPHATE IONS IN 
AQPBOUS EXTRACT 

D-l. REAGENTS 

D-1.1 Etiianolic Potassium Sulphate Solution — a freshly prepared 
solution of 0*018 1 g of potassium sulphate in a mixture of 69 ml of water 
and 31 ml of 95 percent ( vjv j ethanoi. 

8 



tSs78Q3(PartI)-]97$ 

D-l*2 Barium Chloride Solution < — a 25 percent (m/t/ ) aqueous solution 
of barium chloride (BaCla.2H,0 ). 

D-1.3 Dilute Hydrochloric Acid Solution — an approximately 30 per- 
cent {vjv) aqueous dilution of concentrated hydrochloric acid. 

D-1.4 Blue Litmus Paper 

D-l .5 Aqueous Potassium Sulphate Solution — a 0'017 1 percent 
( mju ) aqueous solution of potassium sulphate ( Kg SO 4 ). 

D.2. PROCEDURE 

D-2.1 Pipette 0*25 ml of the edianolic potassium sulphate solution and 
rO ml of barium chloride solution into each of 2 matched test-tubes. Shake 
well, wait for 1 minute and pipette 10 ml of the aqueous extract ( see A-2.2 ) 
of the sample into the first tube and 9 ml of the blank ( see A-2.2.1 ) and 
1 ml of aqueous potassium sulphate solution into the second tube. Test the 
mixture in the 2 tubes with the litmus paper and, if necessary, neutralize 
the mixtures with dilute hydrochloric acid. Then add an additional 0*5 ml 
of dilute hydrochloric acid to each tube and shake. Compare the turbidity 
in the tubes after 5 minutes. 

DO. TEST RESULT 

D-3.1 The sample is deemed to have passed the test if the turbidity in the 
first tube does not exceed that in the second tube. 



APPENDIX E 

[Table 1, Item {lii)] 

METHOD OF LIMIT TEST FOR AMMONIUM IONS IN 
AftUEOUS EXTRACT 

E-l. REAGENTS 

E-1.1 Ammonia-Free Water — Water that shows no colour when a 20-ml 
portion is tested with 2 ml of the alkaline potassium mercuric iodide solution. 

E-1.2 Alkaline Potassium Mercuric Iodide Solution — Dissolve 3*5 g 
of potassium iodide in about 40 ml of water and 1*25 g of mercuric cliloride 
in about 40 ml of water. Mix the solutions and add, with constant stirring, 
a saturated aqueous solution of mercuric chloride until a slight red precipi- 
tate remains. Dissolve 1 2 g of sodium hydroxide in the solution and add a 
little more of saturated mercuric chloride solution and enough of the ammo- 
nia-free water to yield 100 ml. Allow to stand and decant the clear liquid 
for use. 



ISt7803(PartI).197S 

E-13 Ammonium Oiloride Solutioti*— 0*015 percent (mlv) aqueous 
solution of ammonium chlori ie (NH4CI ). 

E-2. PROCaBDURE 

E-2.1 Pipette 1 ml of ammonium chloride solution into the first of two 
matched Nessler tubes and fill the tube up to the 50-ml mark with tiie blank 
solution ( see A-2.2«l ). Fill the second tube up to the 50-ml mark with the 
aqueous sample extract ( see A-2.2 ). Place both tubes on a white tile, add 
1 ml of the alkaline potassium mercuric iodide solution to each tube and 
compare the intensity of the colour developed in each after 2 minutes. 

E.3. TEST RESULT 

E«-3.1 The sample is deemed to have passed the test if the intensity of colour 
in the second tube does not exceed that in the first tube. 



APPENDIX F 

[Table 1, //ew(iv)] 

METHOD OF LIMIT TEST FOR HEAVY METALS IN 
AQUEOUS EXTRACT 

F-l. REAGENTS 

F-l*l Dilated Acetic Acid —Dilute 60 ml of glacial acetic acid with water 
to make 1 000 ml. 

F-1.2 Hydrogen Sulphide Solution — saturated solution of hydrogen 
sulphide made by passing hydrogen sulphide gas ( HsS ) into cold water. 
Store in small, dark amber bottle. 

F-L3 Lead Nitrate Stock Solution ~ Dissolve 159-8 mg of lead nitrate 
in 100 ml of water to which has been added 1 ml of nitric acid, then dilute 
with water to 1 000 ml. Prepare and store this solution in glass containers 
free from soluble lead salts. 

F-L4 Lead Nitrate Solution —Dilute 10 ml of lead nitrate stock solution 
with water to 100 ml. This solution shall be freshly prepared. Each 
millilitre of this solution contains tnc equivalent of 0*01 mg of lead. 

F-2. PROCaSDURE 

F-2*l Pipette 25 ml of the aqueous extract into one of two matched 50-ml 
Nessler tubes and add 2 ml of dilute acetic acid. I]:\to the second Nessler 
tube, pipette 22'5 ml of blank {see A-2«2.1), 2 ml of dilute acetic add

and 2*5 ml of lead nitrate solution. Place the tubes on a white tile and 
add 10 ml of hydrogen sulphide solution. Mix well and allow to stand 
for 10 minutes. View downward and compare the colour. 

F-3, TEST RESULT 

F-3.1 The sample is deemed to have passed the test, if the intensity of 
colour produced in the first tube does not exceed that produced in the 
second tube. "^ 



APPENDIX G 

[Table 1, Item (v)] 

METHOD OF LIMIT TEST FOR CHLORIDE IONS IN 
AQUEOUS EXTRACT 

G-l. REAGENTS \ 

G-1.1 Nitric Acid ( HNOa ) — 6 N, accurately standardized. 

G-1.2 Silver Nitrate Solution — 0*1 N, accurately standardized. 

G-1.3 Sodiain Chloride Solution • — Dissolve 170 mg of sodium chloride 
in water and make up to 1 000 ml. Each millilitrc of this solution is equi- 
valent to 0*103 1 mg of chloride. 

G.2. PROCEDURE 

G-2.1 Pipette 25 ml of aqueous extract ( see A-2.2 ) into one of the two 
matched Ncssler tubes and to the other pipette 1*5 ml of sodium chloride 
solution and 8'5 ml of blank ( see A-2*2*] ). Pipette 1 ml of 6 N nitric acid 
and 1 ml of 0*1 N silver nitrate solution to both the tubes. Mix and 
observe after 5 minutes the turbidity in both the tubes. 

G.3. TEST RESULT 

G-3.1 The sample is deemed to have passed the test if the turbidity in the 
first tube does not exceed that in the second tube.
